passages.note: Senate floor concurrence vote on final passage of the general minimum-wage bill; McGuire is in the Ayes, and 12 of 40 voting members were opposed, so it is not near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: Ayes Allen, Beall, Block, De León, Galgiani, Glazer, Hall, Hancock, Hernandez, Hertzberg, Hill, Hueso, Jackson, Lara, Leno, Leyva, Liu, McGuire, Mendoza, Mitchell, Monning, Pan, Pavley, Roth, Wieckowski, Wolk
passages.tally_quote: Ayes Count 26 Noes Count 12 NVR Count 2

passages.provision_quote: Following the implementation of the minimum wage increase specified in subparagraph (F) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), on or before August 1 of that year, and on or before each August 1 thereafter, the Director of Finance shall calculate an adjusted minimum wage. The calculation shall increase the minimum wage by the lesser of 3.5 percent and the rate of change in the averages of the most recent July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period over the preceding July 1 to June 30, inclusive, period for the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics nonseasonally adjusted United States Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (U.S. CPI-W).
passages.note: Chaptered text: Section 1182.12 raises the general floor on a schedule to "fifteen dollars ($15) per hour" and then adds the annual CPI-W adjustment quoted here, so the bill carries both clauses of the top rung.

rows.reasoning: McGuire voted Aye on final concurrence in SB 3 (2015-2016), a general minimum-wage bill that raises the floor on a schedule to "fifteen dollars ($15) per hour" and then requires the Director of Finance to "calculate an adjusted minimum wage" every August by the U.S. CPI-W, which takes effect the following January 1 with no further legislation. That matches both clauses of the rung "Raise the wage floor and tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation", and the standing index excludes the rung that would "adjust it only when lawmakers vote to".
